nodes.obligation: For a complex polynomial of degree N at least 1, prove that its modulus at any point is at most its supremum on the closed unit disk times max{1, |w|}^N.
reader_obligations: Keep in view that one norm, taken on the unit disk, has to control the polynomial on the whole plane.

anchors.note: The Lean theorem states the bound for every w; the supremum is the definition `a99J07SupNormUnitDisk` rather than a hypothesis. The hypothesis `hN : 1 ≤ N` is never used in the proof body.

nodes.obligation: Define the norm as the supremum of |p| over the closed unit disk, and show it bounds |p| at every point of that disk: the supremum is of a set that compactness of the disk makes bounded above.
reader_obligations: Note that the disk is closed, so the supremum is over a compact set; this is what makes the supremum bound every value on the disk.

anchors.note: The informal proof uses the definition of the norm directly. Lean defines the norm as a supremum of attained values and needs a separate compactness lemma (`apm_a99J07_supNorm_bddAbove`) before `le_csSup` gives the bound in `apm_a99J07_eval_le_supNorm`.

nodes.obligation: Split the claim on the size of |w|: the case |w| at most 1, where the factor max{1,|w|}^N equals 1, and the case |w| greater than 1, where it equals |w|^N and the norm on the disk gives nothing directly.
reader_obligations: Say why the two cases need different arguments: inside the disk the claim is the definition of the norm, outside it the disk says nothing about p(w).

anchors.note: The informal remarks split at |w| <= 1 versus |w| >= 1, which overlap at |w| = 1; Lean splits on ‖w‖ <= 1 and its negation 1 < ‖w‖. The proof-plan lists the two cases as separate strategies without a split node.

nodes.obligation: Case |w| at most 1: |p(w)| is at most the norm by its definition, and max{1,|w|}^N = 1, so the bound holds.
reader_obligations: Check that the right-hand side collapses to the norm in this case, so there is nothing to prove beyond the definition.

nodes.obligation: Introduce the auxiliary polynomial q(z) = z^N p(1/z) (the reflection of p), so that q(1/w) * w^N = p(w); q is a polynomial of degree at most N, hence no issue arises at z = 0.
reader_obligations: See why this is the object to invent: it turns a statement about p outside the disk into a statement about a polynomial inside the disk. Verify the identity q(z) z^N = p(1/z) for z not zero.

anchors.note: The auxiliary object differs in form. The informal proof defines q(z)=z^N p(1/z) and remarks it is analytic on the closed disk; Lean takes Mathlib's `p.reflect N`, a polynomial by construction, with the explicit side condition p.natDegree <= N and no analyticity argument. The proof-plan Stage 3 predicted `Polynomial.reverse`; Lean does not use it.

nodes.obligation: On the unit circle the auxiliary polynomial is bounded by the norm: for |v| = 1, |q(v)| = |p(1/v)| is at most the norm, because 1/v lies on the circle and inside the disk.
reader_obligations: Use that v on the unit circle is not zero and has inverse of modulus one, then apply the bound from the disk to the point 1/v.

anchors.ref: On the unit circle $|z|=1$ we have $|q(z)|=|p(1/z)|\leq\|p\|_\infty$
anchors.note: The informal proof writes |q(z)| = |p(1/z)| on the circle as a remark. Lean proves `(p.reflect N).eval v * v⁻¹^N = p.eval v⁻¹` from `eval₂_reflect_mul_pow` and takes norms, with the side conditions v != 0 and p.natDegree <= N.

nodes.obligation: Boundary to interior for the auxiliary polynomial: for every u in the closed unit disk there is a point v on the unit circle with |q(u)| at most |q(v)| (maximum modulus principle for polynomials).
reader_obligations: Recognize the maximum modulus principle as the tool that lets a bound on the circle bound the polynomial on the whole disk.

anchors.ref: By the maximum modulus principle, $|q(z)|\leq\|p\|_\infty$ for every $|z|\leq 1$
anchors.note: Lean does not cite the maximum modulus principle as a black box. `apm_a99J07_poly_le_boundary` proves a polynomial version: compactness gives a maximiser x on the closed disk; if x is on the circle it is the witness, otherwise the maximum sits in the open disk and `Complex.norm_eqOn_closure_of_isPreconnected_of_isMaxOn` forces the modulus to be constant, so the point 1 is a boundary witness. The lemma returns a boundary point v with |q(u)| <= |q(v)|.

nodes.obligation: Case |w| greater than 1: w is not zero, u = 1/w lies in the closed disk, so |q(u)| is at most the norm by B5 and B6, and the identity p(w) = q(u) w^N gives |p(w)| at most the norm times |w|^N.
reader_obligations: Carry the substitution z = 1/w through the identity, and note where |w| > 1 is used: it makes 1/w a point of the disk and makes max{1,|w|} equal |w|.

anchors.note: The informal proof substitutes z = 1/w in the bound for q. Lean works with an `Invertible w` instance obtained from w != 0 (derived from 1 < ‖w‖), proves ‖w⁻¹‖ <= 1, chains the boundary bound and the disk bound, and rewrites with the identity.

anchors.ref: theorem apm_a99j07: hwlt, hw0, hu, huv, hvb, hqu, hid, heq

anchors.note: The mined gloss reads "If |w| > 1, then |p(w)| ≤ ‖p‖_∞", which drops the factor |w|^N and is false; the quoted source line states the correct bound. Retained as a negative anchoring example.

nodes.obligation: Combine the two cases: every w satisfies one of them, so the bound holds for all complex w.
reader_obligations: Say explicitly that the two cases cover the plane, so the two partial bounds add up to the full claim.

anchors.ref: Combining the two cases proves the inequality
anchors.note: The informal proof has an explicit combining step. Lean has none: the two cases are the branches of one `by_cases` and the theorem is closed in each branch.

profiles.audience: A mathematician who knows the maximum modulus principle and wants the estimate.
profiles.compression: Inside the disk cite the definition; introduce the reflected polynomial in one line and cite the maximum modulus principle for it; substitute z = 1/w. No words on the split or on combining.

profiles.audience: A student who has not seen why a polynomial is reflected to control it outside the disk.
profiles.compression: Show every node; spend the most exposition on why the split is needed, on where the auxiliary polynomial comes from, and on how the boundary bound reaches the interior.

profiles.audience: A reviewer comparing the prose with the compiled Lean proof.
profiles.compression: Do not compress side conditions; expose the compactness lemma behind the supremum, the degree bound on the reflection, the witness form of the maximum modulus lemma, and the invertibility argument.
